maps.for: Where a convention or instruction should live in the CLAUDE.md hierarchy
maps.ask: Who needs this guidance, who owns it, and which files does it follow?
maps.when: You have a new standard, convention or preference and must decide which memory file or folder to put it in.
head: Situation
Right home
Why
rows: Standard for every file, shared with the team and CI
Always loaded in every session, shared via the repo
Standard owned and edited elsewhere in the repo, applies everywhere
References the live file, no copy to drift
Convention that follows a file type across folders
Loads only when matching files are touched
Convention that belongs to one folder only
A multi-step procedure people run on request
Loaded only when invoked, not always on
User-level, not shared via version control
maps.rule: Ask who needs it and which files it follows. Team-wide standards go in the committed project CLAUDE.md, conventions that follow a file pattern across folders go in .claude/rules/ with paths:, and a document someone else owns is referenced with @import, not copied.

maps.for: Instructions ignored or missing for some people: diagnosing which memory file is at fault
maps.ask: Is the guidance actually loaded, and if so, which file is it coming from?
maps.when: Claude ignores a rule, or follows it for one person but not for teammates or CI.
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Not sure which memory files are active
Run /memory to list the files actually in context
Rules work locally but not for teammates
Conventions only in someone's ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md; user level does not travel with the repo
Unwanted habit traced to one person's file
User-level source, or a personal file contradicting the project
Remove or adjust that personal instruction
Unwanted habit from many people, no single source
Fix the path or move the file
The glob doesn't match real files
Conventions span many folders by file type, or apply only to some files
File is loaded, but output follows the rules loosely
CLAUDE.md is huge and hard to maintain
/compact reduces usage; it is not a memory check
maps.rule: Before you change any file or tune a prompt, run /memory to confirm the guidance is loaded. Then fix the habit at the file it comes from: home-folder CLAUDE.md is personal, team conventions go in the committed project CLAUDE.md.

maps.for: Sharing a command with the team versus keeping it personal
maps.ask: Who needs the command, and how will it reach them?
maps.when: A slash command or setting works for you but you must decide whether teammates get it on clone.
head: Who needs it
Right home
Why
rows: Ships with the code, shared via git
Each clone carries its own copy
Only me, every repo, or my own variant
Everyone, and every machine is set up centrally
Always-on team standard, not a command
maps.rule: Shared commands go in each repository's .claude/commands/; personal ones go in ~/.claude/commands/. Only what is committed arrives on clone.

maps.for: Command, skill, path rule or CLAUDE.md: choosing the home by when content should load
maps.ask: Should this load always, when certain files are edited, or only when someone asks?
maps.when: You are packaging a procedure, standard or convention and must pick between a command, a skill, a rule file and CLAUDE.md.
head: Situation
Right home
When it loads
rows: When a matching file is edited
Shared prompt template or routine, small output
On request; versioned and runs in the session
Shared multi-step workflow with verbose or huge working output
When invoked; runs isolated and returns only the result
On-demand workflow that needs tool limits
On request, for one engineer only
maps.rule: Choose the home by when it should load: always (CLAUDE.md), by path (rules with paths:), or on request (commands and skills). Shared heavy-reading routines run in a project skill with context: fork.

maps.for: Controlling a skill: forked context, allowed tools and arguments
maps.ask: Is the problem what the skill can do, how much it puts into my context, or what input it needs?
maps.when: A skill floods the conversation, does something it shouldn't, or needs a value from the user.
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: One skill reads a lot, reports a little; only the summary matters
Verbose step in the main context
Shared on-demand workflow whose detail is needed afterwards
Skill must not use certain tools (for example must not edit files), wherever it runs
Instruction in the skill body is ignored
Turn it into a capability limit with allowed-tools
Block applies to one project, whoever calls the tool
Skill needs a parameter from the user
Ad-hoc exploration in the middle of a task
Explore subagent that returns a summary
Session has grown long over hours
/compact, or a scratchpad plus a fresh session
maps.rule: Fork a skill with context: fork when only its summary matters, and keep it inline when the user will build on its detail. To make a skill unable to do something, restrict allowed-tools in its frontmatter; the limit travels with the skill.

maps.for: Path-scoped rules versus directory CLAUDE.md for file conventions
maps.ask: How are the files this convention covers grouped: by pattern across folders, or inside one folder?
maps.when: A convention applies only to some files and you must choose between a .claude/rules/ file and a folder's CLAUDE.md, or a path rule never applies.
head: Convention applies to
Right home
Loads when
rows: A file type spread across several folders
Editing a matching file, wherever it sits
A task someone runs on request
Root file too long to maintain
Organises it, but still always loads
The glob matches no real files
Fix the glob; check with a matching file and /memory
maps.rule: Conventions for a file pattern across folders go in .claude/rules/ with a paths: glob; one folder's conventions go in that folder's CLAUDE.md. A path rule that never loads usually has a glob that matches nothing.

maps.for: Plan mode, Explore subagent or direct execution for a change
maps.ask: What is still undecided about this change, and how wide is it?
maps.when: You are about to start a code change and must decide whether to plan first, explore first or just edit.
head: Situation
Right approach
Why
rows: Direct execution, then review the diff
Small edit in a big file
Edit on a unique match, not a full rewrite
Many files, several valid designs or unknown dependencies
Direct execution in increments with tests
Tests catch slips; nothing left to design
Need to map unfamiliar code without flooding context, no decision yet
Isolates discovery and returns a summary
Plan mode plus an Explore subagent
maps.rule: Many files plus more than one valid design means plan mode before any edits; a small, clear change goes direct with a diff review. An Explore subagent understands code but does not decide, and tests protect a chosen design but don't choose it.

maps.for: Examples, tests or interview: telling Claude what correct means
maps.ask: What do you already know about the right answer, and what kind of feedback is missing?
maps.when: Iteration keeps going wrong: Claude misreads the task, fixes break other cases, or new cases surprise you every run.
head: What you observe
What is missing
Fix
rows: Requirements unclear or domain unfamiliar; new, unforeseen cases appear each run
Interview pattern: Claude asks questions first
You know the trustworthy outputs, but prose keeps being misread
Concrete input/output examples in the prompt
Fixes break different earlier cases each round, caught by hand
No automatic check of all cases
Write tests first and run them after every edit
Runnable tests already capture the behaviour
Two specific problems keep breaking each other
Send them together in one message
Large or multi-file change with several valid designs
maps.rule: When the requirements are unclear, have Claude interview you before it writes code. Once the right answers are known, iterate against runnable tests if they exist, and use pasted input/output examples only when there are none.

maps.for: One message or several when you have multiple problems
maps.ask: Does the fix for one problem depend on the outcome of another?
maps.when: You have several issues to raise with Claude and must decide whether to send them together or one at a time.
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Problems whose fixes depend on each other
Related by topic, but nothing depends on the outcome
Everything ships in one pull request
Says nothing about how to prompt
Large multi-file change with design choices
maps.rule: Send interacting problems in one message and independent ones separately. Group by dependency, not by topic or pull request.

maps.for: A CI step that hangs, ends empty or behaves differently from local
maps.ask: Which part of the invocation is wrong: mode, permissions, output shape or configuration scope?
maps.when: A Claude Code step in CI hangs, finishes with nothing, or gives different results than on a laptop.
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Job hangs until the job limit, waiting for input
Ends fast, empty, no error, right after a tool request
Tool not permitted, nobody to approve
Allow the needed tools for the CI run
Step finishes, but prose is hard to parse
Review ignores repo conventions, or flags differ from local
Missing project context; criteria only in personal ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md
MCP tools missing in CI only
Review misses flaws in code it just wrote
Step needs no tool loop and can wait hours
maps.rule: A step that hangs is an invocation problem, so use -p first. Non-interactive runs cannot approve anything, so fast, empty, error-free output right after a tool request means the tool wasn't allowed.

maps.for: Getting output in the shape its reader needs: schema, forced tool or format examples
maps.ask: Who reads the output, a program or a person, and through which interface?
maps.when: Claude's output is hard to use downstream: a script can't parse it, the layout varies, or a value is wrong.
head: Situation
Right mechanism
Why
rows: Valid JSON in your named fields, set at generation
Your own app calls the Messages API and must always get one shape
Tool with a JSON schema, forced via tool_choice
The turn must be that tool call
JSON + schema, then the script posts
People read it; layout and detail vary
Output parses but a value is wrong, and time is available
Validate in code, retry with the specific errors appended
Schemas stop syntax errors, not semantic ones
Nullable field, route to a person
Retries can't find what isn't there
Need loud failure when a contract changes
maps.rule: Prose is for people; schemas are for programs. --output-format json gives valid JSON and --json-schema gives your JSON, so constrain at generation when a consumer has a fixed contract.

maps.for: Where CI-specific instructions live versus repo-wide ones
maps.ask: Who needs these instructions: every session, one CI job, one developer, or some files?
maps.when: You need to give a CI job instructions and must decide whether they belong in CLAUDE.md or the job itself.
head: Who needs it
Right home
Why
rows: Every session in the repo, CI and laptops
maps.rule: Ask who needs the rule. Everyone working in the repository means project CLAUDE.md; one job means that job's prompt.

maps.for: Automated review misses things: reviewer, criteria or size
maps.ask: Is the miss caused by who reviews, what they are told to look for, or how much they review at once?
maps.when: An automated code review in CI misses flaws, raises false positives, or rates severity inconsistently.
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Misses flaws only in code the same session wrote
Independent reviewer misses one kind of flaw
Many false positives in a vague category
maps.rule: If a reviewer misses problems only in code it wrote, separate the reviewer. Add criteria once the reviewer is independent.

maps.for: Configuring several CI jobs: real-time, batch and turn limits per job
maps.ask: Is this job bound by latency, by cost, or does it need a tool loop?
maps.when: Several CI jobs share one Claude configuration and their needs pull in opposite directions.
head: Job type
Right setting
Why
maps.rule: Configure latency-bound, on-demand and cost-bound jobs separately. Use batch only for single-pass work; it can't run tool loops.
